prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability for the taking is not in dispute; the case will turn entirely on how much of Korman's cost-approach damages figure the factfinder credits given the State's serious reliability challenge to the blanket 65-75% depreciation applied across the whole 17-acre remainder. Expect a result meaningfully above the $74,429 commissioners' award and likely in the range of Korman's $451,377 computed damages, with some risk of a haircut for the unsupported blanket-depreciation methodology and some chance of recovery closer to the owners' full $1,000,000 ask given the well-corroborated circulation/access damage and two already-won evidentiary rulings (Property Owner Rule testimony and exclusion of post-taking revenue evidence).

outcome.description: After a three-day jury trial in October 2018 the jury awarded $508,548 (exactly the owners' appraiser Korman's cost-approach figure and the low end of the owners' requested range), against the State's requested $74,875-$96,206 and the special commissioners' $74,429; judgment was rendered on the verdict. The Austin Court of Appeals affirmed on March 5, 2021, holding Korman's functional-obsolescence testimony admissible and the exclusion of post-taking revenue evidence not reversible. No attorney's fees in a Texas condemnation award.
